_comment: Sources the owner reported the map was missing, and what now finds each KIND of miss. A seed is one reported URL; its class names the kind of site it is, and _classes says which generator finds that kind from now on, so a miss is fixed once for its class and not only for itself. resolution.state: configured (the host is in a *_sources.json config), annual (a hand-checked entry in annual_sources.json, read every run by mapsee_ingest_annual.py), held (deliberately waiting, with a dated reason), declined (an editorial no: in a _not_included map, or a dated reason here), pending (not yet resolved; a pending seed older than 30 days is a WARN line in test_seeds.py, a ::warning:: annotation under GitHub Actions, and a failure when MAPSEE_TODAY is set). URLs only: never a contact address, which on a small organiser's site is usually a person's own mailbox. Checked by test_seeds.py, no network.

prose-only annual festival on an organis.generator: catalog_mentions.py (named-event mentions in configured feeds, daily in curate-catalog.yml, queued in mention_queue.json) feeding hand-checked entries in annual_sources.json, read every run by mapsee_ingest_annual.py

seeds.why: Short Run Comix Festival, Seattle: free, one day (2026-11-07 11:00-18:00 at the Seattle Design Center), and never on the map. It publishes its date only as WordPress prose on its own site, and no discovery backend starts from a festival's organiser. A configured feed named it a month ahead: The Seattle Public Library's Trumba feed carried 'The Public Life of Comics' (2026-11-08), 'in coordination with the 14th annual Short Run Comix Festival, taking place on Saturday, November 7th ... at Seattle Design Center', and nothing read named events out of ingested rows.
seeds.class: prose-only annual festival on an organiser's own site

resolution.reason: Hand-checked into annual_sources.json; catalog_mentions.py finds the next one of its kind from the feeds we already read (the SPL row above is in mention_queue.json, state configured).
